clue.text: River so long pilots use these to communicate

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for river
the Spanish farewell, used in English as a casual goodbye

explanation.surface: A river runs on so far that pilots must radio to stay in touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft crews talk to air traffic control over two-way wireless sets.

clue.text: Standard tirade that's patently offensive

parts.note: a standard is a banner or flag
a rant is a long angry outburst

explanation.surface: A conventional angry speech that is obviously insulting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like an adjective meaning ordinary, but here it is the noun for a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Something glaring and shamelessly obvious in its wrongness is described with this adjective, as in a blatant breach.

clue.text: Healthy dog that wasn't attached to early movies

definitions.text: that wasn't attached to early movies

parts.note: sound means healthy, as in 'sound in mind and body'
to dog someone is to follow or trail them

explanation.surface: A fit hound that was never used in the early days of cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' reads as an animal but works as a verb meaning to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Early silent films had no recorded audio strip, so this accompaniment was not yet joined to them.

clue.text: Mean policy adjusted minor's pay

indicators.note: something adjusted has been altered, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A stingy rule has altered how much young workers are paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb, but it is the adjective for stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsimony is extreme thrift, a policy of being stingy with money.

clue.text: Part in tragedy, like King Lear

indicators.note: a part in a word means a run of its letters sits inside it

parts.note: letters two to five of this word

explanation.surface: A role in a Shakespearean tragedy, such as King Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Part' a theatrical role; really it says the answer is part of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear is an old king in his dotage, so he is elderly.

clue.text: Inspiration found in the bar when drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests something staggering out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Creative ideas come to someone in the pub once they've had a few.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiration' suggests a creative idea, but it is the literal act of breathing in.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiration is the physical act of drawing air into the lungs, an intake of air.

clue.text: Unfortunate sailor's reason for having no play?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a shipwrecked person left stranded
second meaning, read as two words: the actors are absent, so no show

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the answer into CAST AWAY: with the cast away, no play can go on; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipwrecked mariner stranded on an island is the classic example of someone marooned.

clue.text: Taking everything into account, nothing more to say?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the phrase used for an overall total
second meaning, read literally: the whole story has been related

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal second reading: if everything has been recounted, nothing remains to say.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means 'in total' or 'overall', summing up every item considered.

clue.text: Minimal amount of medicine from doctor prior to surgical procedure

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
OP is short for operation

explanation.surface: A doctor hands out a tiny dose before an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior to' tells you the doctor's letters come first.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid medicines are often measured out in single small globules from a dropper.

clue.text: Land in Africa, having changed regalia

indicators.note: something changed is altered in form, so these letters take another order

parts.note: the letters of this word

explanation.surface: A monarch arrives in an African country after swapping their ceremonial finery.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a large North African country on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Clever and popular mastermind embracing love

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: embracing means holding something within its arms, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a mastermind is a brilliant person
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A brilliant, well-liked schemer who also has a romantic side.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenious means inventive and cleverly original, a close synonym of smart.

clue.text: Delivered wood ahead of time

parts.note: deal is sawn pine or fir timber
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Timber was brought round before the due date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahead of' just places the timber word before the time letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cards are dealt, that is handed out, and a blow can be dealt, so the word means handed over.

clue.text: Second list that's barely adequate

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a ship that lists leans over; cant also means to tilt

explanation.surface: A further inventory that is only just sufficient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' suggests an inventory, but it is the verb for a ship leaning to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means meagre, hardly sufficient in quantity.

clue.text: Book format the writer partly selected

indicators.note: only part of the following words is chosen, so the answer sits inside them

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An author chooses a page layout for their volume.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gospel according to Matthew is the first book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Move weight, creating criterion

parts.note: to move someone emotionally is to touch them
a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: Shifting a heavy object sets the standard for others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' suggests physical shifting, but it means to affect emotionally.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchstone was a stone for testing gold, hence any standard by which things are judged.

clue.text: Scoundrel in favour of dividing money given back

indicators.note: something dividing a thing splits it apart and sits in the gap

parts.note: a rebate is a partial refund
pro means for or in favour of

explanation.surface: A villain approves of splitting up refunded cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled person, a rogue of bad character.

clue.text: Country staged it badly for supplier of home-made products

indicators.note: something done badly is botched and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A nation put on a poor show celebrating its homemade crafts.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage industry is small-scale manufacturing carried out in people's homes.

clue.text: Get ready for pool in fine woollen garment

parts.note: to cash a cheque is to get ready money for it
a mere is a lake or pond

explanation.surface: Prepare for a swim while wearing a soft woolly jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' here is ready money, cash in hand, not preparedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is fine goat's wool, and by extension a sweater knitted from it.

clue.text: Intelligent and fine man not captured on board

parts.note: fine thread is thin
in chess the king is the one piece that is never taken

explanation.surface: A bright, decent fellow who has avoided being caught on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' sounds nautical but means the chessboard, where the king is checkmated, never taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A thinking person, as in 'the thinking man's choice', is one who is intelligent and reflective.

clue.text: Protester runs after small child's vehicle

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a trike is a tricycle
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A demonstrator chases a toddler's tricycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the runs letter at the end, behind the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A striker is a worker who withdraws labour in protest.

clue.text: Feel aggrieved about being put in post again

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
a letter put in the post has been sent

explanation.surface: Someone is bitter at being reappointed to a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' suggests a job, but it is the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter indignation about it.

clue.text: Crowd surrounding one in lift

indicators.note: surrounding means going all round, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a host is a great number, a multitude
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A throng packs round a single person in an elevator.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoist is a device for raising heavy loads, much like a lift.

clue.text: Bound to insert names to be preserved

indicators.note: inserting means placing one thing within another

parts.note: bound means tied up
N is the abbreviation for name, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to add names so they will be recorded for posterity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'obliged to', but 'Bound' alone is the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Food sealed in cans is tinned, a common way of keeping it from spoiling.

clue.text: Perform with female fellow or don? Just the opposite

parts.note: to do a play is to perform it
F is the abbreviation for female
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: Act alongside a woman, a man or a university lecturer, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' tempts as a university tutor, but it is the verb to put on clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To doff a hat is to take it off, the reverse of putting it on.

clue.text: Something produced in bars — heavy metal, for instance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: written scores are divided into measures called bars
second meaning: a genre of rock is one kind of it

explanation.walkthrough: Bars suggest pubs or metal ingots, and heavy metal suggests lead, but both halves point to the art of sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Notated tunes are measured in bars, and heavy metal is one example of a rock genre.

clue.text: China much misrepresented

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown wrongly, so the letters are put in another order

parts.note: the letters of this word

explanation.surface: A great deal of porcelain, or the country itself, has been portrayed falsely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang a china is a mate, so a close friend or pal.

clue.text: Present as means to make novel acquisition, say

definitions.text: Present as means to make novel acquisition, say

parts.words: Present as means to make novel acquisition, say
parts.note: surface reading: a gift that lets someone acquire something new and original
setter's reading: 'novel' is a work of fiction, so the gift buys reading matter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective for new, but it is the noun for a work of fiction; 'say' marks a novel as one example. A book token is a British gift voucher spendable in bookshops.
explanation.definitionFit: This voucher is a common present redeemable for any volume, a novel for instance.

clue.text: Foreign car in neutral, having crashed

indicators.note: a crash wrecks things and leaves them jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of this word

explanation.surface: An imported vehicle left out of gear has had an accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Renault is a French car manufacturer, so its vehicles are imported makes in Britain.

clue.text: Man committed to union securing new funding

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: an engaged man is pledged to marry
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A man devoted to the trade union obtains fresh money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union, but it is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Finance is money provided for a project, the capital that pays for it.
